v.rationale: All three pass their own tests and use the same modern patterns (#[Scope], #[Fillable], queue attributes, retryUntil tied to the claim TTL, failed() clearing the claim). Edge-case probes separated them. impl-1 has the best design for the stated constraints: a shared RateLimited middleware backed by Redis, config-driven settings, onOneServer plus withoutOverlapping, and the most idiomatic tests (withFakeQueueInteractions). Its bugs are a TypeError when the storefront returns missing:null (outside the API contract, but it causes a resend loop), resending on duplicate delivery, and losing an edit made in the same second. impl-2 has the best delivery guard (no resend on duplicate delivery) and is null-safe, but it lacks withoutOverlapping, its claim re-read by timestamp is fragile when runs overlap, it only reacts to 429s, it hardcodes the URL, and its tests use hand-built mocks. impl-3 avoids the same-second lost edit but has a real duplicate-delivery bug that sets synced_at to NULL and over-sends rows edited after the claim. That most directly breaks the task's focus on sending each change exactly once, so it ranks last.
